original_question: Using the same notion of linearly independent immersion, study and classify linearly independent submanifolds of codimension 2.
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem 8: Study and classify linearly independent submanifolds of codimension 2. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's exact open problem in the linearly independent immersion section, and it preserves the intended emphasis on classification in codimension 2 rather than drifting to a broader neighboring question. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))
missing_details: The ambient setting is Euclidean: the paper works with an isometric immersion x:M->E^m of a connected Riemannian manifold M into Euclidean m-space, not with submanifolds of arbitrary ambient manifolds. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

The notion of linearly independent is defined only after assuming x is a k-type immersion with spectral decomposition x=c+x_1+...+x_k, where the x_i are nonconstant E^m-valued eigenmaps of the Laplacian satisfying Delta x_i=lambda_i x_i. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

Because Section 6 starts with a k-type immersion, the stand-alone question should make explicit that the eigenvalues lambda_1,...,lambda_k are mutually distinct, which is the paper's meaning of k-type. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

The subspaces that must be linearly independent are E_i:=span{x_i(p): p in M} subset E^m; this construction is omitted in the draft. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

To make linearly independent fully explicit, one should say that the family E_1,...,E_k is linearly independent as subspaces of E^m, equivalently their sum is direct. This is the paper's operative definition in Section 6. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

Codimension 2 should be spelled out as the case of an n-dimensional submanifold immersed in E^(n+2). The paper's problem is about this Euclidean codimension-2 classification problem in full generality, not only curves or hypersurfaces. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

The nearby context shows the intended benchmark cases: hypersurfaces are already known, and codimension-2 curves are known to be circles, lines, and circular helices. Including this context helps keep the question aligned with the paper's exact scope. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))

No additional algebraic data such as an ambient ring or field, polynomial degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifiers appear in the paper's formulation; the problem is purely differential-geometric in Euclidean space. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))
refined_question: Let x:M^n->E^(n+2) be a k-type isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian manifold into Euclidean space, with spectral decomposition x=c+x_1+...+x_k, where each x_i is a nonconstant E^(n+2)-valued map satisfying Delta x_i=lambda_i x_i and the eigenvalues lambda_1,...,lambda_k are mutually distinct. For each i, set E_i:=span{x_i(p): p in M} subset E^(n+2). Study and classify all codimension-2 Euclidean submanifolds for which the subspaces E_1,...,E_k are linearly independent (equivalently, x is linearly independent in Chen's sense).
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Section 6, Problem 8, so the nearest official target is Problem 8 rather than the neighboring Problem 7 about linearly independent 2-type immersions. The only paper-critical material missing is the definition of linearly independent immersion itself: Section 6 defines it only for k-type Euclidean immersions, using the spectral decomposition introduced in Section 2.1 and the associated subspaces E_i. The same Section 6 also records the already-settled comparison cases (Euclidean hypersurfaces and codimension-2 curves) and mentions Jang's codimension <= 3 partial results, which confirms that the intended question is the Euclidean codimension-2 classification problem in exactly this finite-type/k-type sense. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/873/4133))
